title: NPC
description:
A person standing somewhere who knows something. Distinct from a character entity, which is biography: canon already holds 41 characters, and this is what makes one of them met rather than merely described.

Settlements are information ecosystems, not quest boards. An NPC gives a lead, a word, an old map or a cup of tea -- never a task list.

character.description: Optional character entity id, when this is someone canon already knows. Leave empty for a fisherman who exists only to say one useful thing.

found_at.description: point_of_interest ids where they can be met.

role.description: How they read on meeting -- fisherman, scholar, herder, child. Not a class.

language.description: vocabulary language id they speak. If Varuna lacks the words, what they say arrives incomplete.

knows.description: discovery or field_question ids they can move along. What they offer is a lead, not an answer.

lines.description: What they say, and what it takes to hear it.

requires.description: discovery or vocabulary ids needed before this is said, or understood.

gives.description: discovery, vocabulary or field_question ids this opens.

would_settle.description: Whether this person would join the settlement at the end, if you helped them. Not everyone would: some are rooted where they are, and some would rather not be found. The endgame roster is the people who would, crossed with the discoveries that helped them -- nothing separate is tracked.

descended_from.description: Character ids this person comes from, when the line matters and the person is not that character. Bekh is Mask Family by descent from Kavik across enough generations that the name means little to her -- putting `character_kavik` in `character` would have said she IS him. Found while authoring the Lothal slice, which is what the slice was for.
